How is Flow different from Siri or Google voice typing?
Built-in dictation transcribes what you say, word for word, including every "um," false start, and mid-sentence correction. Then you spend time cleaning it up. Flow uses the most advanced voice technology available to turn what you say into what you meant to write.

Catches your corrections. Say "let's meet at 5... actually 6pm" and built-in dictation writes all of it. Flow gives you "Let's meet at 6pm."
Formats as you speak. Numbered lists, paragraphs, structured emails. Built-in dictation gives you a wall of text; Flow gives you something ready to send.

Yes. Flow is built to handle a wide range of accents and speaking styles. One tip that makes a real difference: select only the language you're speaking right now, and deselect the others.

Flow keeps up with fast talkers and can handle speech as quiet as a whisper. The main thing that matters is your microphone setup: your built-in mic works great, and the closer the mic is to your mouth, the quieter you can speak.

What makes Hunar different
Real workforce conversations are messy. Hunar is built to understand the interruptions, languages, pauses, noise, and context that make them difficult.
Dynamic Interruption Handling
A "yes" mid-call can be a backchannel or a real answer to a question. The difference lies in the context of the conversation, not in the audio activity itself.
We trained our interruption models on how human recruiters actually handle these moments, built specifically for code-mixed, noisy phone conversations.
Audio Regeneration Model
People decide to interrupt before the words come out. So when an agent stops and resumes, it can't pick up from the exact word where it was interrupted. It has to return to the last point that carried meaningful context for the listener.
We built a model that finds that exact resumption point, learned from how human recruiters recover and continue mid-conversation.
Human-like Latency
Our agents respond within 700–900 ms, the natural rhythm at which people expect a reply in conversation.
Anything faster feels like a scripted IVR. Anything slower, and callers begin to drop off. This latency is deliberately engineered.
Maker-Checker Accuracy
Language models hallucinate in live conversations. The real risk isn't the hallucination itself, it's the downstream action that silently breaks because of it.
A second agent reviews every completed call, extracting exactly the information your downstream systems need. This maker-checker loop holds our output accuracy at 90–95%.
